newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania president clears foreign land ownership.
newsitem.headline: Romania president clears foreign land ownership.

text.p: Western businessmen operating in Romania hailed on Wednesday the promulgation of a new law on foreign land ownership, but said more action was needed to improve the business climate in the Balkan country.

"The new law is part of a series of milestones which the new authorities need to pass to demonstrate their conviction that the way of reform and changes is absolutely essential for the successful development of the country," an executive of a major Western company operating in Romania told Reuters.

Under the law, promulgated by President Emil Constantinescu on Wednesday, foreign-owned local companies or firms with partly foreign capital "can acquire the right of property and other real rights for land plots necessary to develop their activity, during their existence here."

The new bill is part of an ambitious reform programme by the country's centrist government and puts an end to almost six years of footdragging over the issue of granting foreigners the right to own land in Romania.

The new bill amends a 1991 foreign investment law which gave foreigners land ownership rights only through local companies having at least one Romanian shareholder. It will become effective after its publication in the Official Gazette.
The former leftist government, ousted in elections last November, had taken no firm stand on the issue and trumpeted the slogan "We don't sell out our country to foreigners".
During debates in parliament on the bill last month, the leftists attacked the document, saying it would harm Romania's national interests and territorial integrity.
"The new authorities should also step up privatisation, which is a key issue, and tackle the improvement of the overall tax burden on businesses," another Western businessman said.
Romania hopes foreign investment will pick up this year as the new government has pledged to support foreign investors by boosting facilities, granting tax cuts and fighting red tape.
Total direct foreign investment since the 1989 overthrow of communist rule has totalled around $2.3 billion, one of the lowest levels in the region.
